questions.question_text:
The displacement in metres of a particle moving along a line is given by $x(t) = 4t^3 - 5t^2 + 8t - 12$ for $t \ge 0$.
What is the velocity function $v(t)$?

options.why: Differentiates $5t^2$ incorrectly by omitting the multiplication by power $2$.
Fails to multiply coefficient $4$ by power $3$ when differentiating $4t^3$.
Multiplies coefficients by power but fails to reduce powers of $t$ by $1$.

questions.question_text:
A particle moves so that its displacement $x$ in metres after $t$ seconds is $x(t) = 2t^3 - 9t^2 + 7$.
What is the velocity of the particle at $t = 4\text{ s}$?

options.why: Evaluates displacement $x(4) = 2(64) - 9(16) + 7 = -9$ instead of velocity.
Evaluates $6(16) - 18(4)$ with arithmetic error or omits second term.
Calculates $18(4) - 6(16)$ with reversed subtraction order.

questions.question_text:
A particle moves with displacement $x = t^2 - 10t + 16$ metres for $t \ge 0$.
At what time is the particle at rest, and what is its displacement then?

options.why: Finds when particle is at origin $x = 0$ rather than at rest $v = 0$.
Assumes displacement must be zero when the particle is at rest.
Uses coefficient $10$ directly as the time instead of solving $2t - 10 = 0$.

questions.question_text:
A particle's displacement is $x(t) = t^2 - 7t + 10$ metres.
What is the velocity of the particle the first time it passes through the origin ($x = 0$)?

options.why: Evaluates velocity at the second passage through origin $t = 5\text{ s}$ where $v(5) = +3\text{ m/s}$.
Evaluates initial velocity $v(0) = -7\text{ m/s}$ instead of velocity at origin.
Confuses passing through the origin $x=0$ with being at rest $v=0$.

questions.question_text:
A remote-control car moves in a straight line with displacement $x(t) = 15t - 3t^2$ metres.
What is its initial velocity?

options.why: Assumes initial velocity must be zero without evaluating derivative at $t = 0$.
Evaluates the acceleration instead of the initial velocity.
Calculates $15 - 3 = 12$ by substituting $t = 1$ into a difference of coefficients.

questions.question_text:
A particle moves according to $x(t) = 2t^3 - 15t^2 + 36t - 8$ metres.
At what times is the particle instantaneously at rest?

options.why: Factors $t^2 - 5t + 6$ incorrectly using factors of $6$ with wrong sum.
Finds the midpoint or zero of acceleration instead of the two rest times.
Solves $36 - 30t = 0$ incorrectly or guesses roots.

questions.question_text:
A particle moves along a straight line with displacement $x(t) = \dfrac{1}{3}t^3 - 4t$ metres for $t \ge 0$.
For which interval of time is the particle moving in the negative direction?

options.why: Finds when the particle is moving in the positive direction ($v > 0$).
Includes negative time values $t < 0$ which are outside the physical domain $t \ge 0$.
Identifies only the boundary time where the particle is at rest.

questions.solution_text:
$v(t) = t^2 - 4$
$\text{Moving in negative direction: } v(t) < 0$
$t^2 - 4 < 0$
$(t - 2)(t + 2) < 0$
$\text{For physical domain } t \ge 0: 0 \le t < 2\text{ s}$

questions.question_text:
A particle moves such that its displacement is $x(t) = t^3 - 12t$ metres for $t \ge 0$.
What is the velocity of the particle when it is at position $x = 16\text{ m}$?

options.why: Confuses the displacement value $16$ with the velocity.
Calculates $3(4)^2 - 24 = 24$ or arithmetic error in evaluating $v(4)$.
Omits subtracting $12$ when evaluating $3t^2 - 12$.

questions.question_text:
“the object is moving left”.
Translate this statement into maths.
The object's displacement is given by the function $s(t)$.
The positive direction is to the right.

options.why: Positive displacement describes position, not the direction of motion.
Negative position does not determine the direction of movement.
A positive displacement derivative represents movement to the right.

questions.solution_text: Velocity is the derivative of displacement. Since right is positive, movement to the left has negative velocity: $\frac{ds}{dt}<0$.
